```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 5,
  out.width = "100%",
  dpi = 150
)
```

`mappingAS` ships with a small occurrence table (`example_occurrences.csv`) for
three Brazilian mountain endemics. Here we screen one of them —
*Prepusa connata* Gardner (Gentianaceae), from the Serra dos Órgãos /
Serra da Mantiqueira region — against **Criterion B** of the IUCN Red List.

The range metrics below run offline, from the points alone. The habitat,
fire, protected-area and report steps are shown as code because they read
MapBiomas / WDPA data over the network.

## 1. Read the occurrences

```{r read}
library(mappingAS)
library(sf)

occ <- read_occurrences(
  system.file("extdata", "example_occurrences.csv", package = "mappingAS")
)

# keep just Prepusa connata
pc <- occ[grepl("Prepusa connata", occ$species), ]
nrow(pc)
```

## 2. Extent of Occurrence and Area of Occupancy

Both are computed on a data-centred equal-area projection, so the areas are in
honest square kilometres regardless of where on Earth the species lives.

```{r metrics}
eoo <- calc_eoo(pc)   # minimum convex polygon
aoo <- calc_aoo(pc)   # occupied 2 km grid cells

c(EOO_km2 = round(eoo$area_km2, 1),
  AOO_km2 = round(aoo$area_km2, 1))
```

## 3. Provisional Criterion B category

`iucn_criterion_B()` turns the two sizes into the provisional category and its
IUCN code notation. **This is a screening result**: it rests on the size
thresholds only and does not replace a formal assessment.

```{r category}
cat_B <- iucn_criterion_B(eoo_km2 = eoo$area_km2, aoo_km2 = aoo$area_km2)
cat_B$code
```

## 4. Map the range

```{r map}
library(ggplot2)

hull_wgs <- st_transform(eoo$hull, 4326)   # the EOO polygon, back in lon/lat

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = hull_wgs, fill = "#2c6e49", alpha = 0.18, colour = "#2c6e49",
          linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_sf(data = pc, colour = "#bc4749", size = 2.4) +
  labs(
    title = expression(italic("Prepusa connata") ~ "— EOO and occurrences"),
    subtitle = sprintf("EOO = %s km² · AOO = %s km² · %s",
                       round(eoo$area_km2), round(aoo$area_km2), cat_B$code),
    x = NULL, y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

## 5. Add habitat conversion, fire and protected areas

The one-call pipeline layers MapBiomas land cover, MapBiomas Fire and the
global WDPA onto the same range. These read data over the network, so the code
is shown rather than run here.

```{r pipeline, eval = FALSE}
res <- assess_species(
  pc,
  year      = 2024,
  mapbiomas = TRUE,   # % converted vs natural land cover within EOO/AOO
  fire      = TRUE,   # burned-area share and fire time series
  wdpa      = TRUE    # overlap with protected areas (global WDPA)
)

res$summary          # one tidy row: EOO, AOO, category, % converted, % burned…
class_table(res)     # full per-land-cover-class breakdown

# Interactive and publication-ready outputs:
map_species(res)         # Leaflet map (points, EOO, AOO, land cover, fire, PAs)
plot_conversion(res)     # converted vs natural, stacked bar
plot_timeseries(cover_timeseries(res))  # land-cover change over time
```

## 6. Write the assessment report

```{r report, eval = FALSE}
# Self-contained HTML (also "txt" or, with the 'officer' package, "docx"):
assessment_report(res, output = "html", file = "prepusa_connata_assessment.html")

# Export the ranges as spatial data (shapefile / GeoPackage) and the
# clipped land-cover raster as GeoTIFF:
export_ranges(res, dir = "ranges", format = "gpkg")
```

## 7. The Shiny application

Everything above — upload, EOO/AOO, habitat conversion, fire, protected areas,
maps, charts, report and exports — is wrapped in an interactive **Shiny app**,
the recommended entry point when you don't want to write code.

```{r shiny, eval = FALSE}
run_app()                      # opens in your browser
run_app(max_upload_mb = 2048)  # allow very large occurrence tables
```

![The mappingAS Shiny application](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lucasbarreirageo/mappingAS/main/man/figures/shiny-app.png){alt="Screenshot of the mappingAS Shiny app"}

> **▶ Run it yourself:** the app runs locally in your browser — install the
> package and call `run_app()` (above). No account or server needed.

## Caveats

The category produced is **provisional and for screening only**. It reflects
the EOO/AOO size thresholds of Criterion B and does **not** include the
sub-conditions (severe fragmentation / few locations, continuing decline,
extreme fluctuation) that a formal IUCN Red List assessment also requires.
